[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! The DB snapshot check also catches schema "dirt" left by DDL-exercising tests (e.g. runtime
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! custom fields ALTERing a table): the snapshot no longer matches, so the next reset rebuilds.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! Residual manual knob: a DESTRUCTIVE change to framework `ensure_*` DDL (a column retyped in
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! place — additive `IF NOT EXISTS` changes self-apply) needs a [`KIT_SCHEMA_VERSION`] bump.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! The fingerprint is per test BINARY (it hashes the models linked into it): binaries linking
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! different module sets still rebuild when they alternate — the win is the dev loop (re-running
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! one binary) and consecutive binaries sharing a module set.
[25](https://docs.rs#25)
[26](https://docs.rs#26)use kigumi_core::{migration_plan, Ctx, ResolvedModel};
[27](https://docs.rs#27)use kigumi_db::{Db, DbError};
[28](https://docs.rs#28)use sqlx::{Connection, PgConnection, Row};
[29](https://docs.rs#29)
[30](https://docs.rs#30)/// Bump when a framework DDL change guarded by `IF NOT EXISTS` cannot self-apply on the TRUNCATE
[31](https://docs.rs#31)/// path (destructive shape changes to `ensure_*` tables; junction-template changes are fingerprinted
[32](https://docs.rs#32)/// verbatim via `m2m_junction_ddl` and self-detect). Additive `CREATE/ADD ... IF NOT EXISTS` changes
[33](https://docs.rs#33)/// do not need a bump.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)pub const KIT_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;
[35](https://docs.rs#35)
[36](https://docs.rs#36)/// One fixed advisory-lock key for the whole kit ("kigumi-test", spelled in hex).
[37](https://docs.rs#37)const LOCK_KEY: i64 = 0x6b69_6775_6d69;
[38](https://docs.rs#38)
[39](https://docs.rs#39)/// The meta table the kit records its fingerprints in (excluded from snapshots and truncation).
[40](https://docs.rs#40)const META: &str = "kigumi_test_meta";
[41](https://docs.rs#41)
[42](https://docs.rs#42)/// A connected, reset test database. Holds the advisory lock for the lifetime of the value — drop
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// it (end of test) and the dedicated lock connection closes, releasing the lock server-side.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)pub struct TestDb {
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    pub db: Db,
[46](https://docs.rs#46)    _lock: PgConnection,
[47](https://docs.rs#47)}
[48](https://docs.rs#48)
[49](https://docs.rs#49)impl TestDb {
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    /// Connects to `DATABASE_URL` and hands back a database reset to a pristine schema. Returns
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    /// `None` (after printing the conventional skip line) when the variable is unset, so tests keep
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    /// the established "skip without a database" behavior:
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    ///
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    /// ```ignore
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    /// let Some(t) = kigumi_test::TestDb::new().await else { return };
[56](https://docs.rs#56)    /// let db = &t.db;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    /// ```
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    ///
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    /// Real failures (bad URL, SQL errors) panic — a broken test database should fail loudly.
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    ///
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// ONE `TestDb` per test, never nested: the advisory lock is per-session and a second `new()`
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// inside the same test would wait forever on the first one's lock.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    pub async fn new() -> Option<TestDb> {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)        let url = match std::env::var("DATABASE_URL") {
[65](https://docs.rs#65)            Ok(u) => u,
[66](https://docs.rs#66)            Err(_) => {
[67](https://docs.rs#67)                eprintln!("skipping: DATABASE_URL not set");
[68](https://docs.rs#68)                return None;
[69](https://docs.rs#69)            }
[70](https://docs.rs#70)        };
[71](https://docs.rs#71)        // The lock connection is dedicated (NOT from the pool): a session advisory lock is released
[72](https://docs.rs#72)        // when its session ends, and a pooled connection outlives the guard by design.
[73](https://docs.rs#73)        let mut lock = PgConnection::connect(&url).await.expect("kigumi-test: connect (lock)");
[74](https://docs.rs#74)        // try-lock loop so a contended (or wedged) lock is attributable instead of a silent hang.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)        loop {
[76](https://docs.rs#76)            let got: bool = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)")
[77](https://docs.rs#77)                .bind(LOCK_KEY)
[78](https://docs.rs#78)                .fetch_one(&mut lock)
[79](https://docs.rs#79)                .await
[80](https://docs.rs#80)                .expect("kigumi-test: advisory lock");
[81](https://docs.rs#81)            if got {
[82](https://docs.rs#82)                break;
[83](https://docs.rs#83)            }
[84](https://docs.rs#84)            eprintln!("kigumi-test: waiting for the kit lock (another test binary is resetting)…");
[85](https://docs.rs#85)            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
[86](https://docs.rs#86)        }
[87](https://docs.rs#87)        let db = Db::connect(&url).await.expect("kigumi-test: connect");
[88](https://docs.rs#88)        prepare(&db).await.expect("kigumi-test: prepare schema");
[89](https://docs.rs#89)        Some(TestDb { db, _lock: lock })
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    }
[91](https://docs.rs#91)}
[92](https://docs.rs#92)
[93](https://docs.rs#93)/// The superuser context every test seeds with.
[94](https://docs.rs#94)pub fn su() -> Ctx {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)    Ctx::new(0, vec![]).sudo()
[96](https://docs.rs#96)}
[97](https://docs.rs#97)
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// The shared insert fixture (the `ins` closure every test used to define): a secured insert as
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// `ctx` with no ACL/rule overlays, unwrapped. Panics on failure — it's a fixture, not the subject.
[100](https://docs.rs#100)pub async fn ins(db: &Db, model: &ResolvedModel, ctx: &Ctx, v: serde_json::Value) -> i64 {
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    db.insert_secured(model, ctx, &[], &[], v.as_object().expect("ins: JSON object"))
[102](https://docs.rs#102)        .await
[103](https://docs.rs#103)        .expect("ins: insert_secured")
[104](https://docs.rs#104)}
[105](https://docs.rs#105)
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// Resets the database for this binary's registered model set (see the module doc for the
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// fingerprint strategy). Public so a bespoke harness can drive it without [`TestDb`] — such a
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// caller MUST hold the kit advisory lock ([`TestDb::new`] does) for the duration, or concurrent
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// binaries can interleave with the whole-schema TRUNCATE/DROP below.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)pub async fn prepare(db: &Db) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    let plan = migration_plan().map_err(DbError::Migration)?;
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    assert!(
[113](https://docs.rs#113)        plan.iter().all(|t| t.model.table != META),
[114](https://docs.rs#114)        "kigumi-test: a model table is named '{META}', which collides with the kit's meta table"
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    );
[116](https://docs.rs#116)
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    sqlx::query(&format!(
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {META} (id INT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1, code_fp TEXT NOT NULL, schema_snap TEXT NOT NULL)"
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    ))
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    .execute(db.pool())
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    .await?;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    let code_fp = code_fingerprint(db, &plan).await?;
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    let stored: Option<(String, String)> = sqlx::query(&format!("SELECT code_fp, schema_snap FROM {META} WHERE id = 1"))
[125](https://docs.rs#125)        .fetch_optional(db.pool())
[126](https://docs.rs#126)        .await?
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        .map(|r| (r.get(0), r.get(1)));
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    // First contact with a database the kit has never built: the reset below wipes EVERY public
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    // table, which is only safe on a dedicated test database. Require one explicit opt-in.
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    if stored.is_none() {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)        let existing = public_tables(db, false).await?;
[132](https://docs.rs#132)        if !existing.is_empty() && std::env::var("KIGUMI_TEST_ALLOW_RESET").is_err() {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)            panic!(
[134](https://docs.rs#134)                "kigumi-test: DATABASE_URL points at a non-empty database the kit has never reset \
[135](https://docs.rs#135)                 ({} tables). If this IS your dedicated test database, set KIGUMI_TEST_ALLOW_RESET=1 \
[136](https://docs.rs#136)                 once; the kit then tracks it via its {META} table.",
[137](https://docs.rs#137)                existing.len()
[138](https://docs.rs#138)            );
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    }
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    let snap_now = schema_snapshot(db).await?;
[142](https://docs.rs#142)
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    match stored {
[144](https://docs.rs#144)        Some((fp, snap)) if fp == code_fp && snap == snap_now => {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            truncate_all(db).await?;
[146](https://docs.rs#146)            ensure_all(db).await?;
[147](https://docs.rs#147)            // An additive framework DDL change self-applies through ensure_*; refresh the record.
[148](https://docs.rs#148)            let snap_after = schema_snapshot(db).await?;
[149](https://docs.rs#149)            if snap_after != snap_now {
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                sqlx::query(&format!("UPDATE {META} SET schema_snap = $1 WHERE id = 1"))
[151](https://docs.rs#151)                    .bind(&snap_after)
[152](https://docs.rs#152)                    .execute(db.pool())
[153](https://docs.rs#153)                    .await?;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)            }
[155](https://docs.rs#155)        }
[156](https://docs.rs#156)        _ => {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            drop_all(db).await?; // meta included — recreated below
[158](https://docs.rs#158)            for t in &plan {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)                db.create_table(&t.model).await?;
[160](https://docs.rs#160)            }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)            for t in &plan {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)                db.create_m2m_relations(&t.model).await?;
[163](https://docs.rs#163)            }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)            ensure_all(db).await?;
[165](https://docs.rs#165)            let snap_after = schema_snapshot(db).await?;
[166](https://docs.rs#166)            sqlx::query(&format!(
[167](https://docs.rs#167)                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {META} (id INT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1, code_fp TEXT NOT NULL, schema_snap TEXT NOT NULL)"
[168](https://docs.rs#168)            ))
[169](https://docs.rs#169)            .execute(db.pool())
[170](https://docs.rs#170)            .await?;
[171](https://docs.rs#171)            sqlx::query(&format!(
[172](https://docs.rs#172)                "INSERT INTO {META} (id, code_fp, schema_snap) VALUES (1, $1, $2) \
[173](https://docs.rs#173)                 ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET code_fp = EXCLUDED.code_fp, schema_snap = EXCLUDED.schema_snap"
[174](https://docs.rs#174)            ))
[175](https://docs.rs#175)            .bind(&code_fp)
[176](https://docs.rs#176)            .bind(&snap_after)
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            .execute(db.pool())
[178](https://docs.rs#178)            .await?;
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        }
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    }
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    Ok(())
[182](https://docs.rs#182)}
[183](https://docs.rs#183)
[184](https://docs.rs#184)/// Every idempotent framework `ensure_*` (schemas + indexes + seeded registries). The index helpers
[185](https://docs.rs#185)/// tolerate absent module tables, so the bundle is safe for any linked-module set.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)async fn ensure_all(db: &Db) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    db.ensure_sequence_schema().await?;
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    db.ensure_event_schema().await?;
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    db.ensure_access_schema().await?;
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    db.ensure_auth_schema().await?;
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    db.ensure_module_schema().await?;
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    db.ensure_setting_schema().await?;
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    db.ensure_view_schema().await?;
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    db.ensure_custom_field_schema().await?;
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    db.ensure_crons().await?;
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    db.ensure_transient_defaults().await?;
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    db.ensure_mail_indexes().await?;
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    db.ensure_stock_indexes().await?;
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    db.ensure_registered_sequences().await?;
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    Ok(())
[201](https://docs.rs#201)}
[202](https://docs.rs#202)
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// The code side of the fingerprint: the DDL of every registered model (name-sorted for stability)
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// plus each Many2many junction shape, hashed server-side (md5 — stable, no extra dependency).
[205](https://docs.rs#205)async fn code_fingerprint(db: &Db, plan: &[kigumi_core::MigrationTarget]) -> Result<String, DbError> {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    let mut targets: Vec<&kigumi_core::MigrationTarget> = plan.iter().collect();
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    targets.sort_by(|a, b| a.model.name.cmp(b.model.name));
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    let mut blob = format!("kit:v{KIT_SCHEMA_VERSION}\n");
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    for t in &targets {
[210](https://docs.rs#210)        blob.push_str(&kigumi_schema::to_ddl(&t.model));
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        blob.push('\n');
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        // Junction DDL verbatim from the SAME function the migration executes — a template change
[213](https://docs.rs#213)        // (FK action, extra column) must change the fingerprint, or IF NOT EXISTS would keep a
[214](https://docs.rs#214)        // stale junction alive through the fast path.
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        for ddl in kigumi_db::m2m_junction_ddl(&t.model) {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            blob.push_str(&ddl);
[217](https://docs.rs#217)            blob.push('\n');
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    let fp: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT md5($1)").bind(&blob).fetch_one(db.pool()).await?;
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    Ok(fp)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)}
[223](https://docs.rs#223)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)/// The database side of the fingerprint: every column and index in the public schema (minus the
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// kit's own meta table), hashed in one round trip. Catches schema dirt (runtime-DDL tests) and
[226](https://docs.rs#226)/// verifies a TRUNCATE-only reset is landing on the schema the last full build produced.
[227](https://docs.rs#227)async fn schema_snapshot(db: &Db) -> Result<String, DbError> {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    let snap: String = sqlx::query_scalar(&format!(
[229](https://docs.rs#229)        "SELECT md5(COALESCE(string_agg(x, '|' ORDER BY x), '')) FROM ( \
[230](https://docs.rs#230)             SELECT table_name || '.' || column_name || ':' || data_type || ':' || is_nullable || ':' || COALESCE(column_default, '') AS x \
[231](https://docs.rs#231)             FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name <> '{META}' \
[232](https://docs.rs#232)           UNION ALL \
[233](https://docs.rs#233)             SELECT indexname || '=' || indexdef FROM pg_indexes \
[234](https://docs.rs#234)             WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename <> '{META}' \
[235](https://docs.rs#235)           UNION ALL \
[236](https://docs.rs#236)             SELECT conrelid::regclass::text || '#' || conname || ':' || pg_get_constraintdef(oid) \
[237](https://docs.rs#237)             FROM pg_constraint \
[238](https://docs.rs#238)             WHERE connamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND conrelid::regclass::text <> '{META}' \
[239](https://docs.rs#239)         ) s"
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    ))
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    .fetch_one(db.pool())
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    .await?;
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    Ok(snap)
[244](https://docs.rs#244)}
[245](https://docs.rs#245)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// Every table in the public schema except the kit's meta table and extension-owned relations
[247](https://docs.rs#247)/// (e.g. PostGIS's spatial_ref_sys — truncating extension data breaks the extension, and dropping
[248](https://docs.rs#248)/// it errors outright).
[249](https://docs.rs#249)async fn public_tables(db: &Db, include_meta: bool) -> Result<Vec<String>, DbError> {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    let rows = sqlx::query(
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        "SELECT t.tablename FROM pg_tables t \
[252](https://docs.rs#252)         WHERE t.schemaname = 'public' AND NOT EXISTS ( \
[253](https://docs.rs#253)             SELECT 1 FROM pg_depend d \
[254](https://docs.rs#254)             JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = d.objid \
[255](https://docs.rs#255)             WHERE d.deptype = 'e' AND c.relname = t.tablename AND c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace)",
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    )
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    .fetch_all(db.pool())
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    .await?;
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    Ok(rows
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        .iter()
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        .map(|r| r.get::<String, _>(0))
[262](https://docs.rs#262)        .filter(|t| include_meta || t != META)
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        .collect())
[264](https://docs.rs#264)}
[265](https://docs.rs#265)
[266](https://docs.rs#266)/// One `TRUNCATE t1, t2, … RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` over the whole schema: BIGSERIAL counters
[267](https://docs.rs#267)/// restart (tests assert concrete ids and sequence numbers) and FK order is irrelevant.
[268](https://docs.rs#268)async fn truncate_all(db: &Db) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    let tables = public_tables(db, false).await?;
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    if tables.is_empty() {
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        return Ok(());
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    let list = tables.iter().map(|t| quoted(t)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    sqlx::query(&format!("TRUNCATE {list} RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE")).execute(db.pool()).await?;
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    Ok(())
[276](https://docs.rs#276)}
[277](https://docs.rs#277)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)/// Drops every table in the public schema (meta included) — the full-rebuild path.
[279](https://docs.rs#279)async fn drop_all(db: &Db) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    let tables = public_tables(db, true).await?;
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    if tables.is_empty() {
[282](https://docs.rs#282)        return Ok(());
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    }
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    let list = tables.iter().map(|t| quoted(t)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    sqlx::query(&format!("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {list} CASCADE")).execute(db.pool()).await?;
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    Ok(())
[287](https://docs.rs#287)}
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// Quotes a catalog identifier, doubling embedded quotes (robustness — the framework never
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// generates such names, but the catalog could hold one).
[291](https://docs.rs#291)fn quoted(ident: &str) -> String {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    format!("\"{}\"", ident.replace('"', "\"\""))
[293](https://docs.rs#293)}

# TestDb in kigumi_test - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-test/0.1.0/kigumi_test/struct.TestDb.html

```
pub struct TestDb {
    pub db:
```
[Db](https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_db/struct.Db.html),
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

A connected, reset test database. Holds the advisory lock for the lifetime of the value — drop it (end of test) and the dedicated lock connection closes, releasing the lock server-side.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.db)

`db: `[Db](https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_db/struct.Db.html)## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Connects to `DATABASE_URL` and hands back a database reset to a pristine schema. Returns
`None` (after printing the conventional skip line) when the variable is unset, so tests keep
the established “skip without a database” behavior:

Real failures (bad URL, SQL errors) panic — a broken test database should fail loudly.

ONE `TestDb` per test, never nested: the advisory lock is per-session and a second `new()`
inside the same test would wait forever on the first one’s lock.

# KIT_SCHEMA_VERSION in kigumi_test - Rust

`pub const KIT_SCHEMA_VERSION: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 1;## Expand description

Bump when a framework DDL change guarded by `IF NOT EXISTS` cannot self-apply on the TRUNCATE
path (destructive shape changes to `ensure_*` tables; junction-template changes are fingerprinted
verbatim via `m2m_junction_ddl` and self-detect). Additive `CREATE/ADD ... IF NOT EXISTS` changes
do not need a bump.

# harn-rules-hostlib 0.8.168 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/harn-rules-hostlib/0.8.168

# harn-rules-hostlib

The host capability that exposes the [ harn-rules](https://docs.rs/harn-rules) declarative
rule engine to the Harn language. Part of the

[Rule Engine program](https://github.com/burin-labs/harn/issues/2826)(Epic A,

[harn#2838](https://github.com/burin-labs/harn/issues/2838)).

## Why a separate crate?

`harn-rules` depends on `harn-hostlib` (for the tree-sitter grammars), so the
`rules` builtins **cannot** live inside `harn-hostlib` — that would be a
dependency cycle. This crate sits one level up
(`harn-cli` → `harn-rules-hostlib` → `harn-rules` → `harn-hostlib`) and an
embedder calls [`install`] next to `harn_hostlib::install_default`.

## Builtins (`std/rules` wraps these)

| Builtin | Gate | What |
|---|---|---|
| `rules.search` | read-only | run a rule, return matches with capture bindings |
| `rules.report` | read-only | run report-only, return a `DataTable`(counts + rows) |
| `rules.diagnostics` | read-only | run a declarative rule, return its diagnostics |
| `rules.visit` | read-only (async) | imperative `on_match($node, ctx)`visitor |
| `rules.apply` | write (deterministic-tools) | apply a codemod `fix`; dry-run by default, safety-gated |

A rule is passed as its **TOML source** (`rule`), with either inline `source`
(+ `language`) or a list of `paths`. So an agent can author and run a rule
entirely from `.harn` without recompiling the binary.

## The imperative visitor (`rules.visit`)

[harn#2878](https://github.com/burin-labs/harn/issues/2878) — the native
escape hatch. `rules.visit` runs a rule's matcher and calls a `.harn` visitor
`on_match($node, $ctx)` once per match. The visitor **returns** its report(s)
— `nil`/`false` to skip, `true` to flag with rule defaults, a
`{message, fix, safety, severity}` dict, or a list of them — which become
diagnostics in the same shape `rules.diagnostics` emits. It can compute a
message or fix from the captured metavars, which the declarative form cannot.

Two design points worth knowing:

- **Async, registered directly on the VM.**A- *synchronous*hostlib builtin cannot call a- `.harn`closure (- `Vm::call_closure_pub`is async-only), so- `rules.visit`is an- **async**builtin installed via- `Vm::register_async_builtin`in [- `install`] rather than through the sync- `HostlibRegistry`. It obtains a child VM from its- `AsyncBuiltinCtx`and calls back per match.
- **Returns rather than mutates.**Harn closures capture by value and- `VmValue`has no callable variant carrying captured Rust state, so a mutating- `ctx.report(...)`could not accumulate soundly. Returning the report is both the correct option and the simpler one.

---

# arcstr - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/arcstr/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#better-reference-counted-strings)Better reference counted strings

This crate defines [ ArcStr](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcStr.html), a type similar to

`Arc<str>`, but with a
number of new features and functionality. There’s a list of
[benefits](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcStr.html#benefits-of-arcstr-over-arcstr)in the

`ArcStr` documentation comment which covers some
of the reasons you might want to use it over other alternatives.Additionally, if the `substr` feature is enabled (and it is by default), we
provide a [ Substr](https://docs.rs/struct.Substr.html) type which is essentially a

`(ArcStr, Range<usize>)`
with better ergonomics and more functionality, which represents a shared
slice of a “parent” `ArcStr` (note that in reality, `u32` is used for the
index type, but this is not exposed in the API, and can be transparently
changed via a cargo feature).[§](https://docs.rs#feature-overview)Feature overview

A quick tour of the distinguishing features:

```
use arcstr::ArcStr;
// Works in const:
const MY_ARCSTR: ArcStr = arcstr::literal!("amazing constant");
assert_eq!(MY_ARCSTR, "amazing constant");
// `arcstr::literal!` input can come from `include_str!` too:
const MY_ARCSTR: ArcStr = arcstr::literal!(include_str!("my-best-files.txt"));
```
Or, you can define the literals in normal expressions. Note that these
literals are essentially [“Zero Cost”](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcStr.html#what-does-zero-cost-literals-mean). Specifically, below we
not only avoid allocating any heap memory to instantiate `wow` or any of
the clones, we also don’t have to perform any atomic reads or writes.

```
use arcstr::ArcStr;
let wow: ArcStr = arcstr::literal!("Wow!");
assert_eq!("Wow!", wow);
// This line is probably not something you want to do regularly,
// but causes no extra allocations, nor performs any atomic reads
// nor writes.
let wowzers = wow.clone().clone().clone().clone();
// At some point in the future, we can get a `&'static str` out of one
// of the literal `ArcStr`s too. Note that this returns `None` for
// a dynamically allocated `ArcStr`:
let static_str: Option<&'static str> = ArcStr::as_static(&wowzers);
assert_eq!(static_str, Some("Wow!"));
```
Of course, this is in addition to the typical functionality you might find in a
non-borrowed string type (with the caveat that there is explicitly no way to
mutate `ArcStr`).

It’s an open TODO to update this “feature tour” to include `Substr`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [format](https://docs.rs/macro.format.html)
- Conceptually equivalent to `ArcStr::from(format!("...", args...))`.
- [literal](https://docs.rs/macro.literal.html)
- Create a const `ArcStr``ArcStr`require no heap allocation, can be freely cloned and used interchangeably with`ArcStr`s from the heap, and are effectively “free”.
- [literal_](https://docs.rs/macro.literal_substr.html)- substr
- `feature = "substr"`: Create a- `const`- `Substr`

---

# harn_hostlib - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-hostlib/^0.8/

## Expand description

`harn-hostlib`: opt-in host builtins for code intelligence (tree-sitter,
repo scanning, deterministic indexing) and tool execution (search, file
I/O, git, process lifecycle, file watcher).

This crate is the Rust home of two classes of optional host capabilities:

- **Code intelligence**—- `ast/`,- `code_index/`,- `scanner/`,- `fs_watch/`.
- **Deterministic tools**—- `tools/`(search, fs, git, process).

These don’t belong inside `harn-vm` — pulling tree-sitter grammars,
ripgrep, and `notify` into the VM would balloon the footprint of every
pipeline that doesn’t index host code. Instead, this crate exposes a
single [ HostlibCapability](https://docs.rs/trait.HostlibCapability.html) trait. Embedders such as

`harn-cli`’s ACP
server) compose the modules they need via [and wire the resulting builtins into the VM through](https://docs.rs/struct.HostlibRegistry.html)

`HostlibRegistry`[/](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html#method.register_builtin)

`harn_vm::Vm::register_builtin`[.](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html#method.register_async_builtin)

`harn_vm::Vm::register_async_builtin`[§](https://docs.rs#status)Status

The AST, scanner, code-index, and deterministic-tool surfaces are
implemented. `fs_watch/` still registers its public contract with
[ HostlibError::Unimplemented](https://docs.rs/error/enum.HostlibError.html#variant.Unimplemented) handlers. Module names, method names,
and JSON schemas under

`schemas/` are the source of truth for hostlib
request/response compatibility, so they must stay stable while module
bodies evolve.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [HostlibError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.HostlibError.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- AST host capability.
- [code_](https://docs.rs/code_index/index.html)- index
- Code index host capability.
- [embed](https://docs.rs/embed/index.html)
- Text-similarity / embedding host capability.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error type for hostlib host calls.
- [fs](https://docs.rs/fs/index.html)
- Session-scoped staged filesystem mode.
- [fs_](https://docs.rs/fs_snapshot/index.html)- snapshot
- Per-tool-call filesystem snapshots — Gemini-style `/restore`primitives.
- [fs_](https://docs.rs/fs_watch/index.html)- watch
- File-system watch host capability.
- [host_](https://docs.rs/host_env_custody/index.html)- env_ - custody
- Shared host-environment custody contracts.
- [process](https://docs.rs/process/index.html)
- Process abstraction used by the deterministic process tools.
- [sandbox](https://docs.rs/sandbox/index.html)
- The runtime arm of the permission primitive: pluggable sandbox
backends that *enforce*a declared policy rather than merely gating tool dispatch.
- [scanner](https://docs.rs/scanner/index.html)
- Repo scanner host capability.
- [schemas](https://docs.rs/schemas/index.html)
- Embedded JSON Schemas for every hostlib host method.
- [secret_](https://docs.rs/secret_store/index.html)- store
- Per-OS secret-store host primitive.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- Deterministic tools capability.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Builtin](https://docs.rs/struct.BuiltinRegistry.html)- Registry
- Mutable collector each capability writes into during `register`.
- [Hostlib](https://docs.rs/struct.HostlibRegistry.html)- Registry
- Composes capabilities and emits VM registrations.
- [Registered](https://docs.rs/struct.RegisteredBuiltin.html)- Builtin
- One registered builtin. The name is what Harn scripts call (e.g.
`hostlib_ast_parse_file`);`module`and`method`are the canonical schema-directory coordinates (`schemas/<module>/<method>.request.json`).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Hostlib](https://docs.rs/trait.HostlibCapability.html)- Capability
- One module’s worth of builtins. Kept tiny on purpose: capabilities exist purely so tests can reason about the surface without booting a VM, and so embedders can opt into individual modules.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_default.html)- default
- Convenience: build a `HostlibRegistry`populated with every capability the crate ships, register them on the supplied VM, and return the registry so callers can introspect (e.g. for schema-drift tests).

---

# harn_lint - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-lint/^0.8/

## Expand description

Harn’s lint crate. The public surface is intentionally narrow: a
handful of `lint_*` entry points, the diagnostic and options types,
and a couple of small utility functions reused by other crates. All
walk state, rule dispatch, and source-aware rule implementations
live in sibling modules.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [native](https://docs.rs/native/index.html)
- C-compatible ABI for native lint rule libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lint](https://docs.rs/struct.LintDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- A lint diagnostic reported by the linter.
- [Lint](https://docs.rs/struct.LintOptions.html)- Options
- Extra options for source-aware lint rules (path-aware rules, opt-in
rules like `require-file-header`).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Lint](https://docs.rs/enum.LintSeverity.html)- Severity
- Severity level for lint diagnostics.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD.html)- COMPLEXITY_ - THRESHOLD
- Default cyclomatic-complexity threshold. Callers can override via
`LintOptions::complexity_threshold``[lint].complexity_threshold`in`harn.toml`). Chosen to match Clippy’s`cognitive_complexity`default and sit between ESLint (20) and gocyclo (30); Harn’s scorer counts`&&`/`||`per operator, so real-world Harn functions score a notch higher than in tools that only count control-flow nodes.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_VARIANT_BRANCH_THRESHOLD.html)- TEMPLATE_ - VARIANT_ - BRANCH_ - THRESHOLD
- Default threshold; see [`template_variant_branch_threshold`] in`harn_cli::config::LintConfig`. Picked to match the issue’s stated default (#1669).
- [GENERATED_](https://docs.rs/constant.GENERATED_HARN_SUFFIX.html)- HARN_ - SUFFIX
- The filename suffix that marks a machine-generated Harn source file:
`<name>.generated.harn`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [collect_](https://docs.rs/fn.collect_selective_import_names.html)- selective_ - import_ - names
- Extract all function names that appear in selective import statements
(`import { foo, bar } from "module"`).
- [derive_](https://docs.rs/fn.derive_file_header_title.html)- file_ - header_ - title
- Derive the title shown inside the autofix’s file-header block. Falls back to a generic “Module.” when no path is available. Only the first letter is capitalized — not every word — per the header style.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_generated_path.html)- generated_ - path
- True if `path`names a machine-generated Harn file (`*.generated.harn`).
- [lint](https://docs.rs/fn.lint.html)
- Lint an AST program and return all diagnostics.
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_diagnostics_from_type_diagnostics.html)- diagnostics_ - from_ - type_ - diagnostics
- Convert type-checker diagnostics tagged as lint rules into ordinary lint diagnostics so CLI/editor callers can share rule filtering, rendering, and autofix plumbing.
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_prompt_template.html)- prompt_ - template
- Lint a single `.harn.prompt`template source. Returns the diagnostics produced by the template-specific lint rules (`template-provider-identity-branch`,`template-variant-explosion`).
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_config.html)- with_ - config
- Lint an AST program, filtering out diagnostics for disabled rules.
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_config_and_source.html)- with_ - config_ - and_ - source
- Lint an AST program, optionally using the original source for source-aware rules.
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_cross_file_imports.html)- with_ - cross_ - file_ - imports
- Lint with cross-file import awareness. Functions named in
`externally_imported_names`are exempt from the unused-function lint even without local references.
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_module_graph.html)- with_ - module_ - graph
- Lint with cross-file import awareness driven by `harn_modules::ModuleGraph`
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_options.html)- with_ - options
- Lint with cross-file import awareness plus extra `LintOptions`
- [lint_](https://docs.rs/fn.lint_with_source.html)- with_ - source
- Lint an AST program with source-aware rules enabled.
- [simplify_](https://docs.rs/fn.simplify_bool_comparison.html)- bool_ - comparison
- Simplify a boolean comparison expression like `x == true`→`x`.
- [type_](https://docs.rs/fn.type_diagnostic_lint_disabled.html)- diagnostic_ - lint_ - disabled
- Returns true when a type diagnostic is a lint diagnostic disabled by the caller’s lint configuration.

# harn_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-parser/^0.8/

Single source of truth for builtin function signatures used by the parser
and runtime VM: identifier resolution, typo suggestions, return-type
inference, static arity & per-arg type checks, runtime arity & type
enforcement, and lint awareness all consult the registry through the
lookup / is_builtin helpers.

Canonical mappings between typed harness.<sub>.* methods and the
ambient builtin names that still back capability classification,
lint migrations, and runtime dispatch.

A single argument to an attribute. Positional args have name = None;
named args use name: Some("key"). Values are restricted to
compile-time metadata expressions by the parser (literal scalars,
identifiers, lists, dicts, and call-shaped sentinels).

A single argument in a Node::HitlExpr call. name is Some when
the caller used named-arg syntax (e.g. quorum: 2); positional
arguments leave it as None and rely on the kind’s parameter order.

Install the process-global signature registry. Called once by the driver
(CLI, LSP, lint, serve, dap) at startup. Test harnesses that build a Vm
via harn_vm::stdlib::stdlib_probe_vm() inherit the install through that
helper.

If node is an AttributedDecl, returns (attrs, inner); otherwise
returns an empty attribute slice and the node itself. Use at the top
of any consumer that processes top-level statements so attributes
flow through transparently.

Names sourced only from the parser’s hand-written static fallback tables
(not the driver-installed #[harn_builtin] registry). Lets cross-crate
drift guards assert the static tables don’t overlap with macro-published
or runtime_only builtins.

---

# harn_rules - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-rules/^0.8/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#harn-rules)harn-rules

The declarative structural rule engine for Harn — the Rust core that
powers `harn rules` / lint / codemod surfaces. A **rule** describes
*what to match* (a pattern snippet, a node kind, or a regex) and
optionally *how to rewrite* it (a `fix`); the engine compiles that rule
against the tree-sitter machinery in [ harn_hostlib::ast](https://docs.rs/harn-hostlib/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_hostlib/ast/index.html) and produces

[es with metavariable bindings.](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.RuleMatch.html)

`RuleMatch`This crate delivers the **atomic matching tier** (#2832), the
**relational + composite algebra** (#2833), the **predicate + rewrite
layer** (#2834), and the **safety + idempotency gate** (#2835):

- `model`- `RuleNode`- `pattern`/- `kind`/- `regex`, relational- `inside`/- `has`/- `follows`/- `precedes`, composite- `all`/- `any`/- `not`/- `matches`) plus- `where`/- `transform`/- `fix`and- `utils`.
- `pattern`- `$VAR`metavariable lifting, unification, literal patterns, and typed- `$VAR:kind`placeholders).
- `evaluator`- utility-rule reuse).

- `constraint`- `where`predicates on captured metavars (regex, comparison, recursive sub-pattern, and Harn-only semantic filters).
- `transform`- `replace`/- `substring`/- `convert`) before fixing.
- `fix`- `fix`template interpolation and format-preserving splice.
- `engine`- `Rule`- `CompiledRule::apply`- `CompiledRule::auto_apply`- `CompiledRule::apply_checked`- `Diagnostic`
- `recipe`- `ScanningRecipe`- `run_recipe`
- `report`- `DataTable`
- `loader`
- semantic capture metadata — Harn captures gain resolved binding identity and simple static type labels when the local syntax provides them.

The whole-project scan lifecycle (#2836) layers onto this surface.

```
use harn_rules::{Rule, CompiledRule};
let rule = Rule::from_toml_str(
    r#"
    id = "destructure-default"
    language = "typescript"
    fix = "{ $KEY: $SRC }"
    [rule]
    pattern = "$SRC?.$KEY ?? $DEFAULT"
    "#,
).unwrap();
let compiled = CompiledRule::compile(&rule).unwrap();
let matches = compiled.run("const a = cfg?.timeout ?? 30;").unwrap();
assert_eq!(matches[0].bindings["KEY"].text, "timeout");
```

# harn_vm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-vm/^0.8/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#harn-vm)harn-vm

The Harn compiler, virtual machine, standard library, provider/LLM layer, orchestration runtime, and host bridge.

[§](https://docs.rs#stability)Stability

This crate is consumed both by the in-tree surfaces (`harn-cli`,
`harn-serve`, the LSP and DAP) and by external embedders. The intended
embedding entry points are `Vm`, `Harness`, `compile_source`, and the
`llm`, `orchestration`, `agent_events`, `agent_sessions`, `config`, and
`security` modules. Other public items exist primarily for in-workspace use
and may change between minor releases; anything marked `#[doc(hidden)]` is
an implementation detail with no stability guarantee. The crate follows the
workspace version and is pre-1.0, so the public surface may still evolve.

- Per-dispatch ceilings on outbound *call counts*— MCP tool calls and Postgres queries — mirroring the LLM cost/token budgets in [`crate::llm::cost`]. A`.harn`handler exported through`harn-serve`declares`@budget(mcp_calls: 20, pg_queries: 50)`; the dispatcher installs the matching guards for the lifetime of the call. Each charge increments a per-thread counter and, once the ceiling is crossed, raises a structured`BudgetExceeded`-categorised error that adapter codecs render as HTTP 429.

# tempfile - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempfile/^3/

## Expand description

This is a library for creating temporary files and directories that are automatically deleted when no longer referenced (i.e., on drop).

- Use `tempfile()``std::fs::File`
- Use `NamedTempFile::new()`*named*temporary file that can be referred to its path.
- Use `tempdir()`
- Use `spooled_tempfile()`

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

This crate provides several approaches to creating temporary files and directories.
[ tempfile()](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) relies on the OS to remove the temporary file once the last handle is closed.

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`[both rely on Rust destructors for cleanup.](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[§](https://docs.rs#resource-leaking)Resource Leaking

`tempfile` will (almost) never fail to cleanup temporary resources. However `TempDir` and
`NamedTempFile` will fail if their destructors don’t run. This is because `tempfile` relies on
the OS to cleanup the underlying file, while `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on rust
destructors to do so. Destructors may fail to run if the process exits through an unhandled
signal interrupt (like `SIGINT`), or if the instance is declared statically (like with
[ lazy_static](https://github.com/rust-lang-nursery/lazy-static.rs/issues/62)), among other possible reasons.

[§](https://docs.rs#unexpected-file-deletion)Unexpected File Deletion

Most operating systems periodically clean up temporary files that haven’t been accessed recently
(often on the order of multiple days). This issue does not affect unnamed temporary files but
can invalidate the paths associated with named temporary files on Unix-like systems because the
temporary file can be unlinked from the filesystem while still open and in-use. See the
[temporary file cleaner](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners) section for more security implications.

[§](https://docs.rs#security)Security

This section discusses security issues relevant to Unix-like operating systems that use shared temporary directories by default. Importantly, it’s not relevant for Windows or macOS as both operating systems use private per-user temporary directories by default.

Applications can mitigate the issues described below by using [ env::override_temp_dir](https://docs.rs/env/fn.override_temp_dir.html) to
change the default temporary directory but should do so if and only if default the temporary
directory (

[) is unsuitable (is world readable, world writable, managed by a temporary file cleaner, etc.).](https://docs.rs/env/fn.temp_dir.html)

`env::temp_dir`[§](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners)Temporary File Cleaners

In the presence of pathological temporary file cleaner, relying on file paths is unsafe because a temporary file cleaner could delete the temporary file which an attacker could then replace.

This isn’t an issue for [ tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) as it doesn’t rely on file paths. However,

[and temporary directories](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`*do*rely on file paths for

*some*operations. See the security documentation on the

[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[types for more information.](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`Mitigation:

- This is rarely an issue for short-lived files as temporary file cleaners usually only remove temporary files that haven’t been modified or accessed within many (10-30) days.
- Very long lived temporary files should be placed in directories not managed by temporary file cleaners.

[§](https://docs.rs#access-permissions)Access Permissions

Temporary *files* created with this library are private by default on all operating systems.
However, temporary *directories* are created with the default permissions and will therefore be
world-readable by default unless the user has changed their umask and/or default temporary
directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#denial-of-service)Denial of Service

If the file-name randomness ([ Builder::rand_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.rand_bytes)) is too small and/or this crate is built
without the

`getrandom` feature, it may be possible for an attacker to predict the random file
names chosen by this library, preventing temporary file creation by creating temporary files
with these predicted file names. By default, this library mitigates this denial of service
attack by:- Defaulting to 6 random characters per temporary file forcing an attacker to create billions of files before random collisions are expected (at which point you probably have larger problems).
- Re-seeding the random filename generator from system randomness after 3 failed attempts to
create temporary a file (when the `getrandom`feature is enabled as it is by default on all major platforms).

[§](https://docs.rs#early-drop-pitfall)Early drop pitfall

Because `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on their destructors for cleanup, this can lead
to an unexpected early removal of the directory/file, usually when working with APIs which are
generic over `AsRef<Path>`. Consider the following example:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::process::Command;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let temp_dir = tempdir()?;
// Spawn the `touch` command inside the temporary directory and collect the exit status
// Note that `temp_dir` is **not** moved into `current_dir`, but passed as a reference
let exit_status = Command::new("touch").arg("tmp").current_dir(&temp_dir).status()?;
assert!(exit_status.success());
```
This works because a reference to `temp_dir` is passed to `current_dir`, resulting in the
destructor of `temp_dir` being run after the `Command` has finished execution. Moving the
`TempDir` into the `current_dir` call would result in the `TempDir` being converted into
an internal representation, with the original value being dropped and the directory thus
being deleted, before the command can be executed.

The `touch` command would fail with an `No such file or directory` error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a temporary file and write some data into it:

```
use tempfile::tempfile;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file = tempfile()?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
```
Create a named temporary file and open an independent file handle:

```
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
use std::io::{Write, Read};
let text = "Brian was here. Briefly.";
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new()?;
// Re-open it.
let mut file2 = file1.reopen()?;
// Write some test data to the first handle.
file1.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
// Read the test data using the second handle.
let mut buf = String::new();
file2.read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
assert_eq!(buf, text);
```
Create a temporary directory and add a file to it:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let dir = tempdir()?;
let file_path = dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
let mut file = File::create(file_path)?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
// By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
// been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
// the directory will still be deleted when `dir` goes out
// of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
// succeeded.
drop(file);
dir.close()?;
```

# harn_rules_hostlib - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/harn-rules-hostlib/0.8.168/target-redirect/harn_rules_hostlib/

## Expand description

Host capability exposing the `harn-rules` declarative rule engine to
Harn as `rules.search` / `rules.report` / `rules.apply`.

This crate lives outside `harn-hostlib` on purpose: `harn-rules` already
depends on `harn-hostlib` (for the tree-sitter grammars), so the rules
builtins would form a dependency cycle if they lived there. An embedder
(harn-cli, harn-serve) calls [ install](https://docs.rs/fn.install.html) alongside

`harn_hostlib::install_default`.[§](https://docs.rs#builtins)Builtins

- `rules.search`(read-only) — run a rule and return its matches.
- `rules.report`(read-only) — run a rule in report-only mode and return a- `harn_rules::DataTable`
- `rules.diagnostics`(read-only) — run a- **declarative**rule and return its- `harn_rules::Diagnostic`
- `rules.visit`(read-only,- **async**) — the- **imperative**escape hatch: run a rule’s matcher, then invoke a- `.harn`visitor- `on_match($node, $ctx)`once per match. The visitor returns its report(s) —- `nil`/- `false`to skip, a- `{message, fix, safety}`dict, or a list of them — which the engine turns into diagnostics of the same shape- `rules.diagnostics`emits. The visitor has full programmatic control (compute a message/fix from the captured metavars), which the declarative form cannot.
- `rules.apply`(write-gated) — apply a codemod rule’s- `fix`; writes only when- `dry_run: false`- *and*the rule is safe to auto-apply (or- `allow_unsafe: true`). Shares the deterministic-tools gate with the other mutating builtins.

A rule is passed as its TOML source (`rule`), so an agent can author and
run a rule — declarative *or* imperative — entirely from `.harn` without
recompiling the binary.

[§](https://docs.rs#why-rulesvisit-is-async-and-why-it-returns-rather-than-mutates)Why `rules.visit` is async, and why it returns rather than mutates

A *synchronous* hostlib builtin cannot call a `.harn` closure: the VM’s
[ Vm::call_closure_pub](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html#method.call_closure_pub) is async-only. So the visitor is registered as an

**async**builtin (directly on the VM via

[, bypassing the sync](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html#method.register_async_builtin)

`Vm::register_async_builtin`[), which can obtain a child VM from its](https://docs.rs/harn-hostlib/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_hostlib/registry/struct.HostlibRegistry.html)

`HostlibRegistry`[and call back per match.](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/async_builtin/struct.AsyncBuiltinCtx.html)

`AsyncBuiltinCtx`The visitor **returns** its reports instead of calling a mutating
`ctx.report(...)`: Harn closures capture by value, so a Harn-side
accumulator could not collect across calls, and `VmValue` has no callable
variant that carries captured Rust state to embed a stateful `report`
method in `ctx`. Returning is both the sound option and the simpler one.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lint](https://docs.rs/struct.LintCapability.html)- Capability
- The `lint`host capability (#2851): runs the Harn linter for an agent/IDE/cloud caller, returning the same diagnostics the CLI emits.
- [Rules](https://docs.rs/struct.RulesCapability.html)- Capability
- The `rules`host capability.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [install](https://docs.rs/fn.install.html)
- Install the `rules`+`lint`capabilities into a VM. Call this alongside`harn_hostlib::install_default`.

---

## Expand description

`harn_hostlib::install_default`.[§](https://docs.rs#builtins)Builtins

**async**builtin (directly on the VM via

[, bypassing the sync](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html#method.register_async_builtin)

`Vm::register_async_builtin`[), which can obtain a child VM from its](https://docs.rs/harn-hostlib/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_hostlib/registry/struct.HostlibRegistry.html)

`HostlibRegistry`[and call back per match.](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/async_builtin/struct.AsyncBuiltinCtx.html)

[150](#150)fn search_run(args: &[VmValue]) -> Result<VmValue, HostlibError> {
[155](#155)    let dict = first_dict(SEARCH, args)?;
[156](#156)    let rule = compile_rule(SEARCH, &dict)?;
[157](#157)    let files = load_files(SEARCH, &dict)?;
[158](#158)
[159](#159)    let mut matches = Vec::new();
[160](#160)    for file in &files {
[161](#161)        for m in rule.run(&file.source).map_err(|e| backend(SEARCH, &e))? {
[162](#162)            matches.push(match_to_vm(&file.path, &m));
[163](#163)        }
[164](#164)    }
[165](#165)    Ok(dict_vm([
[166](#166)        ("result", str_vm("ok")),
[167](#167)        ("match_count", VmValue::Int(matches.len() as i64)),
[168](#168)        ("matches", VmValue::List(Arc::new(matches))),
[169](#169)    ]))
[170](#170)}

[201](#201)async fn visit_run(ctx: AsyncBuiltinCtx, args: Vec<VmValue>) -> Result<VmValue, VmError> {
[206](#206)    let dict = first_dict(VISIT, &args).map_err(host_err)?;
[207](#207)    let rule = compile_rule(VISIT, &dict).map_err(host_err)?;
[208](#208)    let files = load_files(VISIT, &dict).map_err(host_err)?;
[209](#209)    let visitor = match dict.get("on_match") {
[210](#210)        Some(VmValue::Closure(c)) => c.clone(),
[211](#211)        _ => {
[212](#212)            return Err(VmError::Runtime(format!(
[213](#213)                "{VISIT}: `on_match` must be a function `fn(node, ctx)`"
[214](#214)            )))
[215](#215)        }
[216](#216)    };
[217](#217)
[218](#218)    let default_severity = rule.severity();
[219](#219)    let default_safety = rule.safety();
[220](#220)    let rule_id = rule.id().to_string();
[221](#221)
[222](#222)    let mut vm = ctx.child_vm();
[223](#223)    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
[224](#224)    for file in &files {
[225](#225)        let matches = rule
[226](#226)            .run(&file.source)
[227](#227)            .map_err(|e| host_err(backend(VISIT, &e)))?;
[228](#228)        let file_ctx = ctx_vm(&file.path, file.language, &file.source, &rule_id);
[229](#229)        for m in &matches {
[230](#230)            let node = node_vm(m);
[231](#231)            let ret = vm
[232](#232)                .call_closure_pub(&visitor, &[node, file_ctx.clone()])
[233](#233)                .await?;
[234](#234)            ctx.forward_output(&vm.take_output());
[235](#235)            for report in reports_from_return(ret) {
[236](#236)                diagnostics.push(report_to_diagnostic_vm(
[237](#237)                    &file.path,
[238](#238)                    &rule_id,
[239](#239)                    m.span,
[240](#240)                    report,
[241](#241)                    default_severity,
[242](#242)                    default_safety,
[243](#243)                ));
[244](#244)            }
[245](#245)        }
[246](#246)    }
[247](#247)    Ok(dict_vm([
[248](#248)        ("result", str_vm("ok")),
[249](#249)        ("diagnostic_count", VmValue::Int(diagnostics.len() as i64)),
[250](#250)        ("diagnostics", VmValue::List(Arc::new(diagnostics))),
[251](#251)    ]))
[252](#252)}
[253](#253)
[254](#254)fn apply_run(args: &[VmValue]) -> Result<VmValue, HostlibError> {
[255](#255)    let dict = first_dict(APPLY, args)?;
[256](#256)    let rule = compile_rule(APPLY, &dict)?;
[257](#257)    let dry_run = optional_bool(&dict, "dry_run", true);
[258](#258)    let allow_unsafe = optional_bool(&dict, "allow_unsafe", false);
[259](#259)    let format = optional_bool(&dict, "format", true);
[262](#262)    let files = load_files(APPLY, &dict)?;
[263](#263)
[264](#264)    let auto_applicable = rule.safety().is_auto_applicable();
[265](#265)    let mut entries = Vec::new();
[266](#266)    for file in &files {
[267](#267)        let outcome = rule.apply(&file.source).map_err(|e| backend(APPLY, &e))?;
[268](#268)        let formatted = format && outcome.changed && file.language == Language::Harn;
[272](#272)        let rewritten = if formatted {
[273](#273)            match harn_fmt::format_source(&outcome.rewritten) {
[274](#274)                Ok(canonical) => canonical,
[275](#275)                Err(_) => outcome.rewritten,
[276](#276)            }
[277](#277)        } else {
[278](#278)            outcome.rewritten
[279](#279)        };
[280](#280)        let applied = !dry_run && outcome.changed && (auto_applicable || allow_unsafe);
[283](#283)        if applied {
[284](#284)            std::fs::write(&file.path, &rewritten).map_err(|e| HostlibError::Backend {
[285](#285)                builtin: APPLY,
[286](#286)                message: format!("write `{}`: {e}", file.path.display()),
[287](#287)            })?;
[288](#288)        }
[289](#289)        entries.push(dict_vm([
[290](#290)            ("path", str_vm(file.path.display().to_string())),
[291](#291)            ("changed", VmValue::Bool(outcome.changed)),
[292](#292)            ("applied", VmValue::Bool(applied)),
[293](#293)            ("idempotent", VmValue::Bool(outcome.idempotent)),
[294](#294)            ("formatted", VmValue::Bool(formatted)),
[295](#295)            ("safety", str_vm(format!("{:?}", outcome.safety))),
[296](#296)            ("before", str_vm(&file.source)),
[299](#299)            ("preview", str_vm(rewritten)),
[300](#300)        ]));
[301](#301)    }
[302](#302)    Ok(dict_vm([
[303](#303)        ("result", str_vm("ok")),
[304](#304)        ("dry_run", VmValue::Bool(dry_run)),
[305](#305)        ("auto_applicable", VmValue::Bool(auto_applicable)),
[306](#306)        ("files", VmValue::List(Arc::new(entries))),
[307](#307)    ]))
[308](#308)}
[309](#309)
[310](#310)fn fold_run(args: &[VmValue]) -> Result<VmValue, HostlibError> {
[315](#315)    let dict = first_dict(FOLD, args)?;
[316](#316)    let dry_run = optional_bool(&dict, "dry_run", true);
[317](#317)    let files = load_files(FOLD, &dict)?;
[318](#318)
[319](#319)    let mut entries = Vec::new();
[320](#320)    for file in &files {
[321](#321)        let raw_folded =
[322](#322)            harn_rules::fold::fold_destructure_defaults(&file.source, file.language.name())
[323](#323)                .map_err(|e| backend(FOLD, &e))?;
[324](#324)        let raw_changed = raw_folded != file.source;
[325](#325)        let formatted = raw_changed && file.language == Language::Harn;
[326](#326)        let folded = if formatted {
[327](#327)            match harn_fmt::format_source(&raw_folded) {
[328](#328)                Ok(canonical) => canonical,
[329](#329)                Err(_) => raw_folded,
[330](#330)            }
[331](#331)        } else {
[332](#332)            raw_folded
[333](#333)        };
[334](#334)        let changed = folded != file.source;
[335](#335)        let idempotent = harn_rules::fold::fold_destructure_defaults(&folded, file.language.name())
[336](#336)            .map(|again| again == folded)
[337](#337)            .unwrap_or(false);
[338](#338)        let applied = !dry_run && changed;
[339](#339)        if applied {
[340](#340)            std::fs::write(&file.path, &folded).map_err(|e| HostlibError::Backend {
[341](#341)                builtin: FOLD,
[342](#342)                message: format!("write `{}`: {e}", file.path.display()),
[343](#343)            })?;
[344](#344)        }
[345](#345)        entries.push(dict_vm([
[346](#346)            ("path", str_vm(file.path.display().to_string())),
[347](#347)            ("changed", VmValue::Bool(changed)),
[348](#348)            ("applied", VmValue::Bool(applied)),
[349](#349)            ("idempotent", VmValue::Bool(idempotent)),
[350](#350)            ("formatted", VmValue::Bool(formatted)),
[351](#351)            ("safety", str_vm("BehaviorPreserving")),
[352](#352)            ("before", str_vm(&file.source)),
[353](#353)            ("preview", str_vm(folded)),
[354](#354)        ]));
[355](#355)    }
[356](#356)    Ok(dict_vm([
[357](#357)        ("result", str_vm("ok")),
[358](#358)        ("dry_run", VmValue::Bool(dry_run)),
[359](#359)        ("files", VmValue::List(Arc::new(entries))),
[360](#360)    ]))
[361](#361)}
[362](#362)
[363](#363)fn lint_run(args: &[VmValue]) -> Result<VmValue, HostlibError> {
[368](#368)    let dict = first_dict(LINT_RUN, args)?;
[369](#369)    let source = require_string(LINT_RUN, &dict, "source")?;
[370](#370)    let disabled = optional_string_list(&dict, "disabled");
[371](#371)    let severity_overrides = parse_severity_overrides(&dict);
[372](#372)
[373](#373)    let program = harn_parser::parse_source(&source).map_err(|e| HostlibError::Backend {
[374](#374)        builtin: LINT_RUN,
[375](#375)        message: format!("parse error: {e}"),
[376](#376)    })?;
[377](#377)    let options = harn_lint::LintOptions {
[378](#378)        severity_overrides,
[379](#379)        ..Default::default()
[380](#380)    };
[381](#381)    let diagnostics = harn_lint::lint_with_options(
[382](#382)        &program,
[383](#383)        &disabled,
[384](#384)        Some(&source),
[385](#385)        &std::collections::HashSet::new(),
[386](#386)        &options,
[387](#387)    );
[388](#388)    let items: Vec<VmValue> = diagnostics.iter().map(lint_diagnostic_vm).collect();
[389](#389)    Ok(dict_vm([
[390](#390)        ("result", str_vm("ok")),
[391](#391)        ("diagnostic_count", VmValue::Int(items.len() as i64)),
[392](#392)        ("diagnostics", VmValue::List(Arc::new(items))),
[393](#393)    ]))
[394](#394)}
[395](#395)
[396](#396)fn parse_severity_overrides(
[399](#399)    dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap,
[400](#400)) -> std::collections::HashMap<String, harn_lint::LintSeverity> {
[401](#401)    let mut out = std::collections::HashMap::new();
[402](#402)    if let Some(VmValue::Dict(map)) = dict.get("severity") {
[403](#403)        for (rule, value) in map.iter() {
[404](#404)            if let VmValue::String(s) = value {
[405](#405)                let severity = match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
[406](#406)                    "error" => Some(harn_lint::LintSeverity::Error),
[407](#407)                    "warning" | "warn" => Some(harn_lint::LintSeverity::Warning),
[408](#408)                    "info" => Some(harn_lint::LintSeverity::Info),
[409](#409)                    _ => None,
[410](#410)                };
[411](#411)                if let Some(severity) = severity {
[412](#412)                    out.insert(rule.to_string(), severity);
[413](#413)                }
[414](#414)            }
[415](#415)        }
[416](#416)    }
[417](#417)    out
[418](#418)}
[419](#419)
[420](#420)fn lint_diagnostic_vm(diag: &harn_lint::LintDiagnostic) -> VmValue {
[423](#423)    let severity = match diag.severity {
[424](#424)        harn_lint::LintSeverity::Error => "error",
[425](#425)        harn_lint::LintSeverity::Warning => "warning",
[426](#426)        harn_lint::LintSeverity::Info => "info",
[427](#427)    };
[428](#428)    dict_vm([
[429](#429)        ("code", str_vm(diag.code.as_str())),
[430](#430)        ("rule", str_vm(diag.rule.as_ref())),
[431](#431)        ("message", str_vm(&diag.message)),
[432](#432)        ("severity", str_vm(severity)),
[433](#433)        ("start_byte", VmValue::Int(diag.span.start as i64)),
[434](#434)        ("end_byte", VmValue::Int(diag.span.end as i64)),
[435](#435)        ("line", VmValue::Int(diag.span.line as i64)),
[436](#436)        ("column", VmValue::Int(diag.span.column as i64)),
[437](#437)    ])
[438](#438)}
[439](#439)
[440](#440)fn compile_rule(
[445](#445)    builtin: &'static str,
[446](#446)    dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap,
[447](#447)) -> Result<CompiledRule, HostlibError> {
[448](#448)    let toml = require_string(builtin, dict, "rule")?;
[449](#449)    let rule = Rule::from_toml_str(&toml).map_err(|e| HostlibError::InvalidParameter {
[450](#450)        builtin,
[451](#451)        param: "rule",
[452](#452)        message: format!("invalid rule TOML: {e}"),
[453](#453)    })?;
[454](#454)    CompiledRule::compile(&rule).map_err(|e| HostlibError::InvalidParameter {
[455](#455)        builtin,
[456](#456)        param: "rule",
[457](#457)        message: e.to_string(),
[458](#458)    })
[459](#459)}
[460](#460)
[461](#461)fn load_files(
[465](#465)    builtin: &'static str,
[466](#466)    dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap,
[467](#467)) -> Result<Vec<SourceFile>, HostlibError> {
[468](#468)    if let Some(source) = optional_string(dict, "source") {
[469](#469)        let language_name = require_string(builtin, dict, "language")?;
[470](#470)        let language =
[471](#471)            Language::from_name(&language_name).ok_or_else(|| HostlibError::InvalidParameter {
[472](#472)                builtin,
[473](#473)                param: "language",
[474](#474)                message: format!("unknown language `{language_name}`"),
[475](#475)            })?;
[476](#476)        let path = optional_string(dict, "path").unwrap_or_else(|| "<inline>".to_string());
[477](#477)        return Ok(vec![SourceFile {
[478](#478)            path: PathBuf::from(path),
[479](#479)            language,
[480](#480)            source,
[481](#481)        }]);
[482](#482)    }
[483](#483)
[484](#484)    let paths = optional_string_list(dict, "paths");
[485](#485)    if paths.is_empty() {
[486](#486)        return Err(HostlibError::MissingParameter {
[487](#487)            builtin,
[488](#488)            param: "paths",
[489](#489)        });
[490](#490)    }
[491](#491)    let mut files = Vec::new();
[492](#492)    for path in paths {
[493](#493)        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|e| HostlibError::Backend {
[494](#494)            builtin,
[495](#495)            message: format!("read `{path}`: {e}"),
[496](#496)        })?;
[497](#497)        let Ok(contents) = String::from_utf8(bytes) else {
[498](#498)            continue;
[499](#499)        };
[500](#500)        if let Some(file) = SourceFile::detect(&path, contents) {
[501](#501)            files.push(file);
[502](#502)        }
[503](#503)    }
[504](#504)    Ok(files)
[505](#505)}
[506](#506)
[507](#507)fn match_to_vm(path: &std::path::Path, m: &RuleMatch) -> VmValue {
[508](#508)    let captures: harn_vm::value::DictMap = m
[509](#509)        .bindings
[510](#510)        .iter()
[511](#511)        .map(|(name, b)| (name.clone(), str_vm(&b.text)))
[512](#512)        .collect();
[513](#513)    let capture_metadata = capture_metadata_vm(m);
[514](#514)    dict_vm([
[515](#515)        ("path", str_vm(path.display().to_string())),
[516](#516)        ("text", str_vm(&m.text)),
[517](#517)        ("start_row", VmValue::Int(m.span.start_row as i64)),
[518](#518)        ("start_col", VmValue::Int(m.span.start_col as i64)),
[519](#519)        ("end_row", VmValue::Int(m.span.end_row as i64)),
[520](#520)        ("end_col", VmValue::Int(m.span.end_col as i64)),
[521](#521)        ("captures", VmValue::dict(captures)),
[522](#522)        ("capture_metadata", capture_metadata),
[523](#523)    ])
[524](#524)}

[530](#530)    }

[570](#570)fn capture_metadata_vm(m: &RuleMatch) -> VmValue {

[584](#584)    }

[586](#586)        entries.insert("resolved".into(), resolved_binding_vm(resolved));
[587](#587)    }
[588](#588)    VmValue::dict(entries)

[652](#652)fn report_to_diagnostic_vm(
[655](#655)    path: &Path,
[656](#656)    rule_id: &str,

[674](#674)
[675](#675)fn reports_from_return(ret: VmValue) -> Vec<ReportSpec> {
[679](#679)    match ret {
[680](#680)        VmValue::Nil | VmValue::Bool(false) => Vec::new(),
[681](#681)        VmValue::Bool(true) => vec![ReportSpec::default()],
[682](#682)        VmValue::Dict(d) => vec![report_from_dict(&d)],
[683](#683)        VmValue::List(items) => items.iter().filter_map(report_from_item).collect(),
[684](#684)        _ => Vec::new(),
[685](#685)    }
[686](#686)}
[687](#687)
[688](#688)fn report_from_item(v: &VmValue) -> Option<ReportSpec> {
[689](#689)    match v {
[690](#690)        VmValue::Nil | VmValue::Bool(false) => None,
[691](#691)        VmValue::Bool(true) => Some(ReportSpec::default()),
[692](#692)        VmValue::Dict(d) => Some(report_from_dict(d)),
[693](#693)        _ => None,
[694](#694)    }
[695](#695)}
[696](#696)
[697](#697)fn report_from_dict(d: &harn_vm::value::DictMap) -> ReportSpec {
[698](#698)    ReportSpec {
[699](#699)        message: optional_string(d, "message"),
[700](#700)        fix: optional_string(d, "fix"),
[701](#701)        safety: optional_string(d, "safety").and_then(|s| parse_safety(&s)),
[702](#702)        severity: optional_string(d, "severity").and_then(|s| parse_severity(&s)),
[703](#703)    }
[704](#704)}
[705](#705)
[706](#706)fn parse_severity(s: &str) -> Option<Severity> {
[707](#707)    match s {
[708](#708)        "info" => Some(Severity::Info),
[709](#709)        "warning" => Some(Severity::Warning),
[710](#710)        "error" => Some(Severity::Error),
[711](#711)        _ => None,
[712](#712)    }
[713](#713)}
[714](#714)
[715](#715)fn parse_safety(s: &str) -> Option<Safety> {
[716](#716)    match s {
[717](#717)        "format-only" => Some(Safety::FormatOnly),
[718](#718)        "behavior-preserving" => Some(Safety::BehaviorPreserving),
[719](#719)        "scope-local" => Some(Safety::ScopeLocal),
[720](#720)        "surface-changing" => Some(Safety::SurfaceChanging),
[721](#721)        "capability-changing" => Some(Safety::CapabilityChanging),
[722](#722)        "needs-human" => Some(Safety::NeedsHuman),
[723](#723)        _ => None,
[724](#724)    }
[725](#725)}
[726](#726)
[727](#727)fn json_to_vm(value: &serde_json::Value) -> VmValue {
[728](#728)    match value {
[729](#729)        serde_json::Value::Null => VmValue::Nil,
[730](#730)        serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => VmValue::Bool(*b),
[731](#731)        serde_json::Value::Number(n) => n
[732](#732)            .as_i64()
[733](#733)            .map(VmValue::Int)
[734](#734)            .unwrap_or_else(|| VmValue::Float(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0))),
[735](#735)        serde_json::Value::String(s) => str_vm(s),
[736](#736)        serde_json::Value::Array(items) => {
[737](#737)            VmValue::List(Arc::new(items.iter().map(json_to_vm).collect()))
[738](#738)        }
[739](#739)        serde_json::Value::Object(map) => VmValue::dict(
[740](#740)            map.iter()
[741](#741)                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), json_to_vm(v)))
[742](#742)                .collect::<harn_vm::value::DictMap>(),
[743](#743)        ),
[744](#744)    }
[745](#745)}
[746](#746)
[747](#747)fn first_dict(
[752](#752)    builtin: &'static str,
[753](#753)    args: &[VmValue],
[754](#754)) -> Result<Arc<harn_vm::value::DictMap>, HostlibError> {
[755](#755)    match args.first() {
[756](#756)        Some(VmValue::Dict(dict)) => Ok(dict.clone()),
[757](#757)        Some(VmValue::Nil) | None => Ok(Arc::new(harn_vm::value::DictMap::new())),
[758](#758)        Some(_) => Err(HostlibError::InvalidParameter {
[759](#759)            builtin,
[760](#760)            param: "params",
[761](#761)            message: "expected a dict argument".into(),
[762](#762)        }),
[763](#763)    }
[764](#764)}
[765](#765)
[766](#766)fn require_string(
[767](#767)    builtin: &'static str,
[768](#768)    dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap,
[769](#769)    key: &'static str,
[770](#770)) -> Result<String, HostlibError> {
[771](#771)    match dict.get(key) {
[772](#772)        Some(VmValue::String(s)) => Ok(s.to_string()),
[773](#773)        _ => Err(HostlibError::MissingParameter {
[774](#774)            builtin,
[775](#775)            param: key,
[776](#776)        }),
[777](#777)    }
[778](#778)}
[779](#779)
[780](#780)fn optional_string(dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
[781](#781)    match dict.get(key) {
[782](#782)        Some(VmValue::String(s)) => Some(s.to_string()),
[783](#783)        _ => None,
[784](#784)    }
[785](#785)}
[786](#786)
[787](#787)fn optional_string_list(dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap, key: &str) -> Vec<String> {
[788](#788)    match dict.get(key) {
[789](#789)        Some(VmValue::List(items)) => items
[790](#790)            .iter()
[791](#791)            .filter_map(|v| match v {
[792](#792)                VmValue::String(s) => Some(s.to_string()),
[793](#793)                _ => None,
[794](#794)            })
[795](#795)            .collect(),
[796](#796)        _ => Vec::new(),
[797](#797)    }
[798](#798)}
[799](#799)
[800](#800)fn optional_bool(dict: &harn_vm::value::DictMap, key: &str, default: bool) -> bool {
[801](#801)    match dict.get(key) {
[802](#802)        Some(VmValue::Bool(b)) => *b,
[803](#803)        _ => default,
[804](#804)    }
[805](#805)}
[806](#806)

# install in harn_rules_hostlib - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-rules-hostlib/0.8.168/harn_rules_hostlib/fn.install.html

`pub fn install(vm: &mut `[Vm](https://docs.rs/harn-vm/0.8.168/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/harn_vm/vm/state/struct.Vm.html))## Expand description

Install the `rules` + `lint` capabilities into a VM. Call this alongside
`harn_hostlib::install_default`.

Struct LintCapability   Copy item path  Source  `pub struct LintCapability;`Expand description The `lint` host capability (#2851): runs the Harn linter for an
agent/IDE/cloud caller, returning the same diagnostics the CLI emits.

Returns the “default value” for a type.

From <T> for U

Returns a styled value derived from `self` with the foreground set to
`value`.

This method should be used rarely. Instead, prefer to use color-specific
builder methods like `red()``green()`

# bitlist 0.0.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitlist/0.0.5

# bitlist

Word-sized bit list implementation with bigint functionality.

Main type of this crate is `BitList` - dynamic bitset storing up to 57 bits (on 64-bit target) inline without allocation, heap allocating for more bits.

Size of `BitList` is equal to `size_of::<usize>()`, type is also niche optmizated so `Option<BitList>` is same size as `BitList`.

The crate is under developement, it's missing documentation and examples. But is otherwise usefull and most of the methods do what you expect. Please also checkout `BitsIter` type as it is not only an iterator but also has methods to effeciently find bits in sparse lists.

---

# rand - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rand/^0.10/

## Expand description

Random-number generators and samplers

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
// rand::random() supports many common types:
println!("Uniform i8 sample: {}", match rand::random() {
    0i8 => "zero",
    i if i > 0 => "positive",
    _ => "negative",
});
// Ranged sampling:
use std::f32::consts::PI;
println!("Angle: {} degrees", rand::random_range(-PI..PI));
```
See also [The Book: Quick Start](https://rust-random.github.io/book/quick-start.html).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [rand_core](https://docs.rs/rand_core/0.10.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rand_core/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [distr](https://docs.rs/distr/index.html)
- Generating random samples from probability distributions
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Convenience re-export of common members
- [rngs](https://docs.rs/rngs/index.html)
- Random number generators and adapters
- [seq](https://docs.rs/seq/index.html)
- Sequence-related functionality

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [RngReader](https://docs.rs/struct.RngReader.html)- `std`
- Adapter to support `std::io::Read``TryRng`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Crypto](https://docs.rs/trait.CryptoRng.html)- Rng
- A marker trait for securely unpredictable infallible RNGs
- [Fill](https://docs.rs/trait.Fill.html)
- Support filling a slice with random data
- [Rng](https://docs.rs/trait.Rng.html)
- Trait for infallible random number generators
- [RngExt](https://docs.rs/trait.RngExt.html)
- User-level interface for RNGs
- [Seedable](https://docs.rs/trait.SeedableRng.html)- Rng
- A random number generator that can be explicitly seeded.
- [TryCrypto](https://docs.rs/trait.TryCryptoRng.html)- Rng
- A marker trait over `TryRng`
- [TryRng](https://docs.rs/trait.TryRng.html)
- Base trait for random number generators and random data sources

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [fill](https://docs.rs/fn.fill.html)- `thread_rng`
- Fill any type implementing `Fill`
- [make_](https://docs.rs/fn.make_rng.html)- rng - `sys_rng`
- Construct and seed an RNG
- [random](https://docs.rs/fn.random.html)- `thread_rng`
- Generate a random value using the thread-local random number generator.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_bool.html)- bool - `thread_rng`
- Return a bool with a probability `p`of being true.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_iter.html)- iter - `thread_rng`
- Return an iterator over `random()`
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_range.html)- range - `thread_rng`
- Generate a random value in the given range using the thread-local random number generator.
- [random_](https://docs.rs/fn.random_ratio.html)- ratio - `thread_rng`
- Return a bool with a probability of `numerator/denominator`of being true.
- [rng](https://docs.rs/fn.rng.html)- `thread_rng`
- Access a fast, pre-initialized generator

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#bitlist)bitlist

Word-sized bit list implementation with bigint functionality.

Main type of this crate is `BitList` - dynamic bitset storing up to 57 bits (on 64-bit target) inline without allocation, heap allocating for more bits.

Size of `BitList` is equal to `size_of::<usize>()`, type is also niche optmizated so `Option<BitList>` is same size as `BitList`.

The crate is under developement, it’s missing documentation and examples. But is otherwise usefull and most of the methods do what you expect. Please also checkout `BitsIter` type as it is not only an iterator but also has methods to effeciently find bits in sparse lists.
